findings.title: String subclasses can escape the canonical identifier postcondition
findings.description: canonical_id accepts a str subclass after validating its underlying text and returns that same subclass instance. A subclass whose stored value is one canonical UUID but whose __str__ returns a different valid canonical UUID is therefore accepted, is reported canonical by is_canonical_id, and leaves the API as an identity-substituting object rather than a trusted plain wire string. It is also rejected later by canonical_json, which requires exact strings, so the public primitives disagree about whether the returned value is canonical.
findings.required_change: Require exact str inputs or reconstruct and return a trusted exact str without invoking overrideable subclass methods. Add regressions proving that identifier string subclasses cannot substitute identity and that canonical_id always returns an exact str accepted by canonical serialization.

findings.title: Time subclasses can substitute the parsed instant and canonical output
findings.description: The time API accepts str and datetime subclasses and invokes overrideable methods on them. A str subclass can override endswith and slicing so parse_utc validates one RFC 3339 value but returns a different instant. A datetime subclass can override utcoffset, astimezone, or isoformat so normalize_utc returns the untrusted subclass and canonical_utc emits a different valid timestamp or arbitrary non-RFC text. These paths violate UTC normalization and canonical-format postconditions.
findings.required_change: Do not invoke overrideable subclass behavior while establishing canonical time values. Reject unsupported subclasses or copy from trusted base-type state, ensure normalize_utc returns an exact UTC datetime, validate the final canonical_utc postcondition, and add substitution and noncanonical-output regressions for both str and datetime subclasses.

findings.title: Overrideable Mapping.items defeats canonical serialization and hashing
findings.description: Canonical JSON admits arbitrary Mapping implementations and trusts their overrideable items method even though the declared JsonValue object type is dict and arrays and scalar types use exact-type admission. A dict subclass can keep one stored payload while returning a different payload, or different payloads on successive calls, from items. canonical_json and canonical_sha256 then serialize or hash substituted and potentially nondeterministic content for the same stored value.
findings.required_change: Restrict canonical JSON objects to exact dict values, or establish an equally strong non-overrideable representation boundary, and add regression coverage proving mapping subclasses cannot substitute or vary canonical payload content.
